changes.title: The Foundry becomes the parent system
changes.body: Money Radar, repo archaeology, Wolfram optimisation, venture generation and the business command centre now share one evidence and outcome loop.

changes.title: Wolfram AgentTools moved today
changes.body: The agent-to-Wolfram bridge is now a priority integration seam for computational evaluation and optimisation.

changes.title: Eight venture candidates now have simulation baselines
changes.body: Each idea has a Monte Carlo revenue range and probability measures. Actual outcomes remain empty until money is genuinely received.

changes.title: Frontend becomes the observability layer
changes.body: Every report, repo, prompt, venture assumption, company thesis and learning event should be inspectable from one interface.

prompts.title: GITHUB GOLD MINE → BILLION-SCALE PRODUCT DISCOVERY → WOLFRAM INVENTION ENGINE
prompts.summary: Find under-commercialised open-source technology, inspect it deeply, combine capabilities into new products, validate demand and optimise architecture/economics with Wolfram.

prompts.title: X10THINK MULTI-MODE INTELLIGENCE LAYER
prompts.summary: Route a problem through deliberately different reasoning modes, cross-examine their outputs and synthesise the strongest evidence-backed conclusion.

prompts.title: UNIVERSAL EXACT SITE CLONE → OPEN-SOURCE AI ENGINEERING → WOLFRAM OPTIMISATION ENGINE
prompts.summary: Reconstruct authorised sites from measurements, infer implementation, source reusable open technology, verify fidelity and mathematically optimise the rebuilt system.

prompts.title: AUTONOMOUS BUSINESS COMMAND CENTRE
prompts.summary: Create, operate, observe, fund, improve and kill a portfolio of autonomous AI businesses through one transparent control plane.

prompts.title: DARWIN VENTURE EVOLUTION ENGINE
prompts.summary: Represent ventures as genomes, run experiments, measure economic fitness, mutate architecture and preserve useful traits from failed ventures.

prompts.title: CONTEXT-ADAPTIVE CHEAT CODE ORCHESTRATOR
prompts.summary: Choose the best prompt modes automatically from the task, run them in useful sequence and prevent ritualistic overuse of irrelevant modes.

prompts.title: REPOSITORY GOLD
prompts.summary: Find obscure but high-leverage repositories, then inspect architecture, exact modules, licences, maintenance and integration seams.

prompts.title: REPO → STARTUP
prompts.summary: Turn reusable repository primitives into differentiated products and new technical stacks rather than superficial wrappers.

prompts.title: PAPER → PRODUCT
prompts.summary: Translate research or technical ideas into working product primitives, experiments and commercial architectures.

prompts.title: AI ARCHITECTURE
prompts.summary: Design explicit agent/tool/state graphs, choose what should be probabilistic vs deterministic and define failure/recovery behaviour.

prompts.title: AGENT ECONOMICS
prompts.summary: Model agent actions as capital-allocation decisions using expected value, time, compute, uncertainty, downside and reusable learning.

prompts.title: CLOSED-LOOP SELF LEARNING
prompts.summary: Observe, hypothesise, test, measure, backtest and promote policy changes only when outcomes improve.

prompts.title: INTERFACE INVENTION
prompts.summary: Design interfaces around the decision a user must make, progressive disclosure and cognitive throughput rather than decorative dashboards.

prompts.title: FIRST DOLLAR
prompts.summary: Optimise a business experiment for legitimate time-to-first-revenue, then turn successful fulfilment into a repeatable loop.

prompts.title: NOT A WRAPPER
prompts.summary: Reject generic LLM wrappers and force identification of proprietary loops, data, infrastructure, decision engines or distribution advantages.

prompts.title: MARKET GAP DISCOVERY ENGINE
prompts.summary: Find evidence-backed gaps where demand, workarounds, pricing pain or technological change reveal an underserved job.

prompts.title: TOTAL INVENTION ENGINE
prompts.summary: Move from fragment or observation to theory, market evidence, technology reconnaissance, architecture, category creation and build plan.

prompts.title: MOST EFFECTIVE DESIGN ENGINE
prompts.summary: Optimise UI and workflow around human cognition, usability, goal attainment and the actual behaviours required for success.

prompts.title: BUILD MODE
prompts.summary: Stop at the first executable architecture, implement the smallest real system, test it and use failures to choose the next change.

ventures.name: Repo-to-Revenue Foundry
ventures.thesis: Continuously find useful OSS primitives, compile them into narrow commercial tools and test demand automatically.
ventures.nextTest: Pick one repo combination and pre-sell one concrete outcome before full build.

ventures.name: Autonomous Website Revenue Rescue
ventures.thesis: Detect broken conversion paths, generate a measured repair, show proof and sell the fix as an outcome.
ventures.risk: Outbound quality, consent, proving causal uplift
ventures.nextTest: Run on a small public sample, quantify defects and validate willingness-to-pay without bulk outreach.

ventures.name: Agent Procurement Hunter
ventures.thesis: Find digital bounties/RFPs/contracts that agents can genuinely fulfil, price them and execute bounded work.
ventures.risk: Eligibility, acceptance, fulfilment quality, platform rules
ventures.nextTest: Collect 100 live opportunities and measure eligible/actionable fraction before bidding.

ventures.name: Public Data Refinery
ventures.thesis: Turn messy public datasets into continuously refreshed niche intelligence feeds with decision-ready outputs.
ventures.risk: Commodity data, niche selection, freshness burden
ventures.nextTest: Build one high-value feed where buyers currently assemble data manually.

ventures.name: AI Stack Cost Optimizer
ventures.thesis: Benchmark an organisation's agent/model workload, route it through cheaper equivalent components and charge from verified savings.
ventures.risk: Access to workloads, measurement, procurement friction
ventures.nextTest: Benchmark one reproducible workload across providers/local models and publish verified savings.

ventures.name: Autonomous Micro-SaaS Foundry
ventures.thesis: Generate many tiny software experiments from observed workflows, kill weak ones and compound reusable infrastructure.
ventures.risk: Distribution and idea quality dominate code generation
ventures.nextTest: Limit to one user type and force demand evidence before each build.

ventures.name: Open-Source Managed Service Arbitrage
ventures.thesis: Find valuable OSS that users struggle to deploy/operate and sell reliable hosted outcomes around it.
ventures.risk: Licence, support load, incumbent hosted version
ventures.nextTest: Find projects with high usage plus repeated deployment pain and no strong hosted offering.

ventures.name: Autonomous QA + Reconstruction Lab
ventures.thesis: Agents compare live interfaces against references/specs, identify fidelity defects and implement verified corrections.
ventures.risk: Authorisation, subjective design quality, proving value
ventures.nextTest: Benchmark against known before/after implementations and quantify defect reduction.

wolfram.method: 20,000-run Monte Carlo per venture using uncertain opportunity volume, conversion, price, gross margin and fixed-cost distributions.
wolfram.caveat: These results depend entirely on stated priors. They become useful only when updated against actual funnel and revenue data.

Alphabet.does: Search, YouTube, advertising, cloud and AI platforms.
Alphabet.why: High-margin intent advertising at enormous scale, YouTube monetisation and growing cloud demand.
Alphabet.moat: Distribution, user intent data, advertiser liquidity, infrastructure and AI research.
Alphabet.lesson: Own a repeated high-intent behaviour, then layer infrastructure and adjacent products around it.

NVIDIA.does: Accelerated-computing chips, systems, networking and the CUDA software ecosystem.
NVIDIA.why: AI training and inference demand makes scarce high-performance compute strategically valuable.
NVIDIA.moat: CUDA ecosystem, hardware/software co-design, developer adoption and supply-chain scale.
NVIDIA.lesson: A software ecosystem can make hardware economics much stronger than hardware alone.

Apple.does: Consumer devices plus services, payments, subscriptions and an integrated software ecosystem.
Apple.why: Premium hardware margins combine with a huge installed base that repeatedly buys high-margin services.
Apple.moat: Brand, distribution, silicon, ecosystem integration and switching costs.
Apple.lesson: A profitable platform compounds when hardware distribution creates recurring software/service revenue.

Microsoft.does: Enterprise software, Azure cloud, security, developer tools, AI and productivity software.
Microsoft.why: Recurring enterprise contracts plus cloud consumption give Microsoft multiple high-margin monetisation surfaces.
Microsoft.moat: Enterprise distribution, identity, developer ecosystem, installed software and cloud scale.
Microsoft.lesson: Distribution into business workflows can be as valuable as model capability.

Meta Platforms.does: Social networks and messaging monetised primarily through digital advertising.
Meta Platforms.why: Massive attention inventory plus increasingly effective ad ranking makes advertiser ROI and margins strong.
Meta Platforms.moat: Network effects, global reach, recommendation systems and advertiser demand.
Meta Platforms.lesson: If an AI system can measurably improve customer acquisition, monetisation can scale extremely quickly.

Broadcom.does: Semiconductors, networking silicon and infrastructure software.
Broadcom.why: AI networking and specialised silicon demand combine with high-margin enterprise software assets.
Broadcom.moat: Deep IP, customer integration, switching costs and mission-critical infrastructure.
Broadcom.lesson: Boring infrastructure with hard technical constraints can be more profitable than visible consumer apps.

Oracle.does: Databases, enterprise software and cloud infrastructure.
Oracle.why: Mission-critical database lock-in, recurring support/software revenue and expanding cloud workloads.
Oracle.moat: Installed enterprise data layer and very high switching costs.
Oracle.lesson: Owning the system of record creates pricing power and durable expansion paths.

IBM.does: Enterprise software, infrastructure, consulting and hybrid-cloud/AI services.
IBM.why: Large enterprise relationships and mission-critical software generate recurring, sticky revenue.
IBM.moat: Enterprise trust, legacy integration depth and regulated-industry relationships.
IBM.lesson: Integration and reliability around AI can be a business even when the core model is commoditised.

Cisco Systems.does: Networking hardware, security and recurring infrastructure software.
Cisco Systems.why: Enterprise networks are mission-critical and increasingly sold with recurring software/security layers.
Cisco Systems.moat: Installed base, channel, interoperability and enterprise trust.
Cisco Systems.lesson: Attach recurring software to indispensable infrastructure.

General Electric.does: Industrial technology businesses with high-value engineered equipment and services.
General Electric.why: Installed equipment creates long-lived service, parts and maintenance economics.
General Electric.moat: Certification, engineering depth, installed base and high switching costs.
General Electric.lesson: The best recurring revenue can originate from assets that customers cannot casually replace.

Micron Technology.why: AI servers require large amounts of high-value memory, with supply constraints amplifying pricing.
Micron Technology.moat: Capital intensity, process know-how and manufacturing scale.
Micron Technology.lesson: Find the constrained component every fast-growing system cannot function without.

SAP.does: Enterprise resource planning and business software.
SAP.why: Core finance, operations and supply-chain workflows are deeply embedded and migrating to recurring cloud contracts.
SAP.moat: System-of-record status, data gravity and organisational switching costs.
SAP.lesson: Deep workflow ownership produces long retention and expansion revenue.

Salesforce.does: CRM, sales, service, data and AI software.
Salesforce.why: Recurring subscriptions sit directly in revenue-generating business workflows.
Salesforce.moat: Customer data, ecosystem, integrations and sales distribution.
Salesforce.lesson: Software closest to revenue can justify higher pricing when it proves ROI.

Adobe.why: Professional workflows rely on category-standard tools sold through subscriptions.
Adobe.moat: File formats, professional habit, ecosystem and brand.
Adobe.lesson: Own the professional workflow and the artefact format around it.

Applied Materials.why: Chipmakers must buy highly specialised tools to increase capacity and process sophistication.
Applied Materials.moat: Extreme technical difficulty, service relationships and process IP.
Applied Materials.lesson: Toolmakers can monetise a boom more reliably than many end applications.

Thermo Fisher Scientific.does: Scientific instruments, laboratory products and services.
Thermo Fisher Scientific.why: Recurring consumables and services attach to a massive installed scientific-instrument base.
Thermo Fisher Scientific.moat: Regulated workflows, distribution breadth and installed equipment.
Thermo Fisher Scientific.lesson: Consumables and services around specialised infrastructure create compounding economics.

Dell Technologies.does: Enterprise and consumer computing, servers, storage and infrastructure.
Dell Technologies.why: AI infrastructure refresh cycles and enterprise purchasing relationships support large volumes.
Dell Technologies.moat: Supply chain, enterprise channel and infrastructure integration.
Dell Technologies.lesson: Distribution and procurement convenience can remain valuable in commoditising hardware markets.

Qualcomm.why: Chip sales are supplemented by high-margin licensing of communications IP.
Qualcomm.moat: Patent portfolio, standards participation and modem expertise.
Qualcomm.lesson: Licensable technical primitives can create revenue independent of operating every end product.

Texas Instruments.why: Thousands of long-lived chips sell into industrial and automotive systems with stable demand.
Texas Instruments.moat: Manufacturing scale, catalogue breadth and design-in longevity.
Texas Instruments.lesson: Huge profitable businesses can be built from many small indispensable components.

NetEase.does: Games, online services and digital content.
NetEase.why: Hit games create high-margin virtual-goods and recurring engagement revenue.
NetEase.moat: Content IP, live operations and player communities.
NetEase.lesson: Digital goods have powerful margins when attached to durable engagement.

rules: Predicted revenue is labelled MODELLED until verified by an actual transaction.
Every experiment records assumption, action, cost, result and prediction error.
A failed venture contributes reusable knowledge before it is killed.
Policy changes must beat the previous policy in backtests or bounded live tests.
Do not optimise proxy metrics when cash, retention or verified user value can be observed.
